items.title: Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi moves Delhi court for copy of FIR against him
items.summary: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi has approached Delhi's Patiala House Court seeking a copy of the first information report (FIR) registered against him by the Delhi Police. The case is likely to be taken up for hearing by Judge Mridul Gupta on Tuesday. Joshi was questioned for nearly nine hours by the Delhi Police Special Cell on September 2 in connection with a case registered against him over his social media activity. Joshi is a retired 1992-batch Indian Posts and Telecommunications Accounts and Finance Service officer who retired as an Additional Secretary-rank official in March 2026. He was allegedly picked up while on a morning walk and taken to the Counter Intelligence unit’s office in New Friends Colony. Police said he was questioned in connection with an FIR registered two days earlier and was released after his statement was recorded. The plea by Joshi has been filed through advocates Aadil Singh Boparai, Ronit Bose and Nikunj Bindal. Note: An initial version of the story described Joshi as an ex-IAS officer. items.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider setting up expert panel for legal education reforms
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Central government to consider setting up an expert body to examine issues concerning legal education in India [Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay v Union of India & Ors] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana held that such a body was particularly relevant in the present era. “This is an important matter. The Union of India should consider it. This is an era of expert bodies. There should be an expert body on legal education,” said CJI Kant. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court made the observation while hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) filed by Advocate Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay. The plea sought the constitution of a Legal Education Commission or expert committee comprising educationists, jurists, retired judges, advocates and professors. It also sought a review of the existing legal education framework, including the syllabus, curriculum and duration of Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) and Master of Laws (LL.M.) courses. items.title: Supreme Court extends tenure of 3 NGT members; AG says 229 tribunal members' tenure extended
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday allowed two Judicial Members and one Expert Member of the National Green Tribunal (NGT) whose once-extended terms expire today to continue in office despite their crossing the retirement age, until fresh member appointments are made. The direction was passed by a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana to ensure that the NGT's functioning is not hampered until new appointments are made to fill vacancies at the tribunal. "In order to ensure that the day-to-day functioning of the National Green Tribunal is not hampered, we direct continuation of the two Judicial Members and one Expert Member as an interim measure till fresh appointments are made in their place," the Court ordered. The order was passed after Attorney General (AG) R Venkataramani apprised the Court of the position concerning vacancies in various tribunals during the transition to a new regime under the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2026 . items.title: Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra sworn in as Punjab & Haryana High Court Chief Justice; Punjab CM skips
items.summary: Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra was sworn in as the Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court by Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Monday morning. Justice Mishra was administered the oath of office despite the Punjab government's opposition to his elevation as the Chief Justice. The State government on Sunday said that the Central government should not have notified Justice Mishra's appointment without awaiting its response on his suitability. While Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann was conspicuous by his absence at the oath ceremony today, his Haryana counterpart Nayab Singh Saini was present. Haryana Governor Prof. Ashim Kumar Ghosh was also present at the ceremony. Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra swearing in ceremony Justice Mishra, who was appointed a judge of the Allahabad High Court in February 2014, has been posted at the Punjab and Haryana High Court since July 2025. He has been serving as the Acting Chief Justice since June. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended Justice Mishra’s elevation on August 6. items.title: Courts must resist rehearing arbitral awards on merits to build global arbitration hub: Darius Khambata
items.summary: If India has to develop as a preferred arbitration seat, courts in the country must resist the temptation to re-hear arbitration disputes on merits, Senior Advocate Darius Khambata said on September 5 . The senior lawyer was speaking at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) Arbitration Week in GIFT City on ‘Rules of Private International Law in International Commercial Arbitration. He explained that non-interference from courts means resisting the temptation to decide the matter. “In arbitration, the justice of the case requires that a court respect the decision of the parties that an arbitral tribunal decides, and not a judge. That's the justice of the case,” he added. Khambata urged courts to explicitly frame challenge grounds immediately instead of re-hearing the entire disputes on merits. “If you have a good judicial ecosystem and a good legislative ecosystem that really makes for a very successful seat,” he said. He also highlighted Singapore’s practice of institutional humility. “With all its success, every single month and year the Singaporeans are thinking of how we can improve? Where have we gone wrong?
